newsitem.title: USA: FoxMeyer unit bankruptcy auction set Nov 6.
newsitem.headline: FoxMeyer unit bankruptcy auction set Nov 6.

text.p: An auction of Foxmeyer Health Corp's bankrupt unit, Foxmeyer Drug Co, and five affiliates will take place Nov 6 in New York, FoxMeyer attorney Martin Sosland said.
Chief Judge Helen Balick of the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Delaware has scheduled a hearing Nov 8 to approve the asset sale.
Balick signed an order Wednesday approving the sale procedure after FoxMeyer amended it at the judge's request from a strung-out bidding process to a standard auction.

A FoxMeyer spokeswoman told Reuters the change "invites more people in and in some ways makes it easier." In the original proposal, McKesson Corp had several days in which to decide whether to top a competing bid by raising its $80 million asset-purchase agreement with FoxMeyer.
The auction on Nov 6 will be at 1030 EDT in the New York offices of FoxMeyer attorneys Weil Gotshal & Manges, Sosland told Reuters.

In addition to a standard auction, the revised procedure now also requires a first overbid of $87 million, or at least $7 million higher than McKesson's offer, and that each subsequent overbid be at least $1 million. The court has approved a $6.5 million termination fee for McKesson if it is not the winning bidder.
The FoxMeyer spokeswoman said the agreement with McKesson would serve as a "blueprint" for any final agreement.

Balick also approved a $30 million loan by McKesson to FoxMeyer's debtor-in-possession financing and "Mckesson has wired the money today," Sosland said. FoxMeyer said last week the funds "will enable FoxMeyer to buy about $100 million of additional inventory and help to revive its business."
FoxMeyer Drug, a wholly owned subsidiary of Dallas-based FoxMeyer Health Corp, is the fourth-largest pharmaceutical and health-care distributor in North America with 2400 employees in 21 states.
